source.publication: 2025 Montana Individual Income Tax Return Form 2 and Form 2 Instructions
source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p13 Line 6, $5,660 subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older; Form 2 PDF p1 line 6; record base.deductions age_65_subtraction

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - standard deduction 17,350.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 32,650.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, although Montana's line 2 would take it). Filing status married filing separately, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 17,350.00; line 3 32,650.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 1 x 5,660.00 = 5,660.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 32,650.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 5,660.00 = 26,990.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 26,990.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 26,990.00 = 1,592.41, less 253 = 1,339.41; line 13 = 1,339.41, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (26,990.00 - 21,100.00 = 5,890.00) = 347.51; bracket tax 1,339.21. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,339.21. The form gives 1,339.41; expected keeps the projection's 1,339.21, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20).
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
